data.name: Cleopas
data.gender_notes: Cleopas is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Greek word κλεοπάς (kleopas), meaning 'glory of the people'. In the New Testament, Cleopas is a disciple of Jesus who appears in the story of the Road to Emmaus. The name Cleopas carries the meaning “Glory of the people” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Cleopas usually hope their child will grow to embody glory of the people and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A name symbolizing the spiritual journey and the glory of following the teachings of Jesus.
data.etymology: Cleopas belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Glory of the people.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Cleopas total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_hebrew.name: קליאופס
in_hebrew.meaning: קליאופס הוא שם שפירושו תהילה לאבא
in_hebrew.long_meaning: קליאופס הוא שם שפירושו תהילה לאבא, והוא מורכב משתי מילים ביוונית: 'קליאוס' שפירושו תהילה ו'אופס' שפירושו אבא. השם קליאופס מוזכר בברית החדשה, בספר לוקס, ככינויו של אחד מתלמידי ישו.

in_greek.name: Κλεόπας
in_greek.long_meaning: Κλεόπας σημαίνει δόξα τω πατρί, δηλαδή δόξα στον πατέρα. Ο Κλεόπας ήταν ένας από τους μαθητές του Ιησού Χριστού, όπως αναφέρεται στο Ευαγγέλιο του Λουκά.

in_latin.name: Cleopas
in_latin.meaning: Cleopas means glory to the father
in_latin.long_meaning: Cleopas is a name that means glory to the father, derived from the Greek words 'kleos' meaning glory and 'papas' meaning father. Cleopas is mentioned in the New Testament, in the book of Luke, as a disciple of Jesus Christ.

in_english.name: Cleopas
in_english.meaning: Glory to the father, a disciple of Jesus Christ
in_english.long_meaning: The name Cleopas is derived from the Greek words 'kleos' meaning glory and 'papas' meaning father. It is a significant name in Christian tradition, as Cleopas was one of the disciples of Jesus Christ, mentioned in the New Testament, specifically in the book of Luke. The name symbolizes devotion and reverence to God the Father.

data.cultural_impact: Cleopas holds significant cultural importance in Christian history, particularly due to his appearance in the New Testament story of the Road to Emmaus. This biblical narrative relates how, after the Resurrection of Jesus, Cleopas and another disciple encountered the Risen Lord on the road to the village of Emmaus. This encounter profoundly impacted their understanding of the events that had transpired and strengthened their faith. Cleopas' role in this story underscores thetransformative power of personal encounters with Jesus, and has been revered through history as an example of unwavering discipleship.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Cleopas holds great significance as it symbolizes the dignity and worth of all people. The Greek root 'kléos', meaning glory, reflects the belief that every person is created in the image and likeness of God and thus possesses inherent worth and dignity. In this sense, the name Cleopas serves as a powerful reminder that each individual has a vital role to play in God's plan for the world and in sharing the Good News of salvation through Jesus Christ. The name, derived from Greek, 'glory of the people', stands as a constant reminder that every person's life has eternal value and importance in the eyes of God.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Cleopas is a Greek form of the name Cleophas, which means "glory of Phoebus". In Christian tradition, Saint Cleopas is identified as one of the two disciples on the road to Emmaus. He represents the hidden or overlooked presence of God in everyday life.

biblical_reference.note: Cleopas is mentioned as a disciple of Jesus Christ in Luke 24:18.

historical_references.reference: Cleopas, one of the two disciples that met Jesus on the road to Emmaus, is believed to be the same person as Cleopas, son of Joseph, mentioned in the New Testament book of Luke (24:13-35).
historical_references.context: Post-Resurrection appearance of Jesus to his disciples

historical_references.reference: Another theory suggests that Cleopas may have been identified with Cleopas, the brother of Simon Peter, mentioned in the New Testament book of Matthew (10:2-4) and Mark (3:16-19).
historical_references.context: Jesus' early ministry and selection of the twelve apostles

modern_usage.modern_context: Cleopas is a modern name of historical significance, primarily associated with early Christian history as one of the two disciples on the road to Emmaus in the New Testament. In modern Egyptian culture, Cleopas is less commonly recognized but can be found in various works of literature and art. Additionally, Cleopas holds significance in biblical tourism, particularly for Christian pilgrims seeking to visit sites associated with the New Testament. On Wikipedia, articles about Cleopas can be found in both English and Egyptian Arabic. On Reddit, there are various threads dedicated to discussing biblical figures, including Cleopas. Lastly, Google Arts & Culture offers virtual tours of various sites associated with Cleopas and other biblical figures.

name_in_real_life.story: Mary Cleopas, a minister in Rome, Italy, shares that their name Cleopas meaning "Glory of the people" has been a constant source of inspiration, guiding them to serve others and live according to Christian values.
